item.description:
• Studio project saves use the default folder while default save folders are enabled; disabling them restores the previous custom folder.

Added

  • Each Studio project in the Clips Library has buttons to open its folder in Finder or delete the Library copy without removing separately saved projects or exported videos.
  • Studio can show a project in Finder after its first save. The switch is off by default; later saves do not open Finder.
  • Studio Recording has its own configurable global shortcut, unassigned by default, in Settings and onboarding on macOS and Windows. Record Video remains an ordinary recording.
  • Open MP4 and MOV files directly in Studio from Finder with **Open With → Tiny Clips**, without changing the default player.
  • The Clips Library has a Studio Projects section for finding and reopening projects and drafts. Agents can open stored projects by ID with `studio.project.open`.
  • Agents can discover unreadable Studio Library projects, including their IDs and readability status, before deleting a damaged copy.
  • Settings → General → Save Location has a **Studio projects folder** for Studio's **Save Project** and **Save Project As**, defaulting to a `Studio` folder inside the video save folder. Projects already saved to a folder keep saving there, and drafts and recordings stay in Studio's own storage. Agents can read it as the read-only `studioProjectFolder` setting.

Changed

  • The macOS Guide is now a feature-first handbook with Capture, Editor, Recording, Studio, Library, Agents, and Help tabs, offline overview drawings, practical walkthroughs, and website documentation links. Help retains your live shortcut reference.
  • Agents can open a specific Guide topic on macOS and Windows with `app.open window=guide guideTopic=studio` (or any of the seven topics), including when the Guide is already open. The command keeps read scope and reports the selected topic.
  • Tiny Clips Studio is generally available on macOS and Windows. What's New no longer presents it as a preview; it introduces Agent Control. Users who previously disabled Studio keep existing projects because upgrade migration disables automatic cleanup until they choose new limits.
  • Agents on macOS and Windows can disable microphone and camera source capture for an individual video or Studio recording with `microphone=false camera=false`, without changing saved preferences or needing settings scope. Enabling requires existing user opt-in and OS permission, without permission prompts. Choices survive countdown, Studio fallback, and restart; recording status reports effective device capture and macOS startup/device errors.
  • Only Screenshot has a global keyboard shortcut by default on macOS; Video, GIF, OCR, direct screenshots, and Stop Recording are optional. Saved bindings are preserved. Stop Recording can be recorded, cleared, or reset in Settings and is active globally only during recording.
  • Shortcuts settings groups Screenshots, Recording, and Text recognition separately from fixed editor, Studio, Clips Library, and navigation references. Onboarding offers Screenshot, Record Video, Studio Recording, and Record GIF, and explains how to stop without a shortcut.
  • Shortcut configuration deliberately remains UI-only; agents continue to use capture and recording commands directly.
  • Studio speed is now a slider from 0.25x to 8x in 0.25x steps, including normal speed without losing the selected range.
  • Agents on macOS and Windows can save a portable Studio project copy through `studio.project.saveCopy` without overwriting existing files.

Fixed

  • Reset All Settings now restores capture and Studio preferences in the running app without a relaunch, including the recording display-sleep preference.
  • **Use default folders** on macOS no longer turns itself off on the launch after installing or resetting settings, and is turned back on once for anyone it was turned off for without choosing a folder. The App Store build shows your Pictures/TinyClips and Movies/TinyClips folders in Settings instead of its sandbox container path.
  • Studio's Save Project folder setting refreshes immediately and preserves spaces in chosen folder names.
  • Pausing an agent-controlled video and withdrawing device consent keeps the take paused on resume. Restart checks consent before discarding the take, including from the floating control.
  • Finder and Clips Library reuse the same Studio edits for an unchanged imported video. Recovering a copied MOV preserves its format.
  • Studio Projects refreshes no longer read every project twice. `editor.open` supports a standard result with a separate file path on both platforms (`resultFormat=standard`).
  • Tall sticky footers no longer repeat during slow scrolling captures on macOS.
  • Scrolling screenshots now keep the lower viewport overlap until the final frame, preventing bottom-floating controls such as Teams' "New messages" badge from repeating throughout the image.
  • Studio drafts made from existing videos now appear in Settings → Studio → Drafts instead of being counted in storage but hidden from the list.
  • macOS Studio Save Project and Save Project As… now work for videos opened from the Clips Library or video editor, in both the Studio and File menus. The video is copied into the project folder; the original is left unchanged.
